verbatims.quote: Four books and a refresh every few hours? I already have fifteen books open in tabs. And line moves aren't money. If you say 'where the money's moving', show me handle or don't say it.
The second I read 'Beat the sportsbooks' I figured it was another Telegram capper. Nobody beats the books long term, that's the whole point.
Honestly I just want my teams' games, the spread at each book, and whether it moved since morning. If it does that without making me sign up first, I'd keep it.
Props tools are the only thing I'd pay for. Hot streaks with no sample size are just bait though, 5 of his last 6 means nothing.
Wait, so I can't actually place a bet in it? Then what's the point. I'd just use the sportsbook app.
The insider directory is where this goes sideways. Who decides who gets listed? Half the blue checks on betting Twitter are selling 80% win-rate Discords.
An AI that won't tell me what to bet is the first AI betting thing I'd actually trust. If it shows the number and when it was pulled, fine, I'd use it.
Free, no picks, no betting. So how do you make money? My guess is sportsbook referral links, and then the whole thing is just an ad.

researcher_note: F won; outcome claims B, H, C backfired with serious and industry. Casuals the only group rating B and H above average. G lost ground with serious bettors (4 books + refresh contradict 'every number'); some sharps called F misleading since line movement isn't money flow. Stale or wrong odds was the top distrust trigger among serious bettors (54 of 63); 56% would pay for nothing.
